answer: Capacity-capped trust graphs resist Sybil attacks by weighting signed peer endorsements through Personalized PageRank from verified anchor nodes. Because outgoing edge weight is strictly bounded, a hollow cluster of self-vouching puppets cannot ripple upward in rank; each accepted identity costs scarce third-party endorsement slots. Influence flows like a river only across earned links, though bribed or compromised anchors can still bridge fake clusters.
